title: Professional and Therapy-Room Games
hook: The third referral looks generous until Rebecca hears how useful its failure would be.
counterintuition: The professional role can hide the helper's payoff. Look at both sides of the exchange before deciding who is stuck and who is benefiting from stuckness.
tryThisNow: Before offering help again, write what would count as the other person using it. If you cannot name that, pause the offer.
keyTakeaway: Helping games stay respectable because help is visible; test whether the offer has a usable path or needs failure to prove the helper tried.

breakdown.fastRead:
"I found another program that might help," Rebecca says, then hears the old script in her own voice. The referral binder is open, a bus pass envelope sits beside the case note screen, and the last two referrals were never used.

I'm Only Trying to Help You can make failure useful to the helper because it proves the helper tried. The help may be real. The trap is that failed help keeps both roles intact.

Rebecca asks which referral the client would actually use and what blocked the last one. Help becomes testable, not impressive.
breakdown.deepRead:
The leather notebook already has three models boxed in blue ink. Matteo is coaching an executive who can discuss attachment, avoidance, and systems thinking for twenty minutes without making one phone call from the call list. The calendar invite for the next session is already accepted.

Psychiatry-style touring uses polished vocabulary to move around the problem rather than through it. Greenhouse is nearby: every feeling behind glass, labeled and watered, never lived.

Matteo asks for one call before the next session.

That request changes the room. Insight is no longer the product by itself. The question becomes whether language produces contact with the avoided act. The professional has to be careful here, because insight can be real and still become shelter. A person can understand themselves beautifully and not move one inch.

The helper is part of the game. I'm Only Trying to Help You begins when Matteo gets paid in continued need while the client gets paid in continued non-action. The clean move is not contempt for language. It is a behavioral criterion.
breakdown.fullRead:
The accessibility office window faces a courtyard full of construction noise. Frida reads the accommodation letter, sees the noise-canceling headphones on the desk, and checks the missed lab safety quiz. The sensory limit is real. The quiz requirement is also real.

The limitation may be real; the game begins when the limitation is used to cover a demand it does not actually touch. Wooden Leg is dangerous when read crudely, because real disabilities and real limits must be respected. The target is not limitation. The target is deployment: using a limitation as a permanent exemption from unrelated accountability.

Frida grants the sensory accommodation and sets a new date for the safety quiz.

You can apply the same care in a workshop. Ben watches a trainee hold digital calipers over a scrap aluminum bar while the measurement worksheet waits. The trainee says, "I am terrible at numbers," and Ben almost takes the calipers back. Rescue would be faster. It would also teach both of them that helplessness works. Ben hands the calipers back and waits for the number to be read aloud.

Some of these names sound harsh because they come from a clinical era with blunt labels. Handle them as structures, not insults. The pattern called Stupid is not low ability. It is the social performance of inability that lowers expectations and recruits rescue. The pattern called Psychiatry is not treatment. It is specialized vocabulary used as a tour bus around change.

Chiara sees Greenhouse in a therapy group. A circle of chairs surrounds a tissue box and a handwritten feeling list. Someone says, "I am noticing activation around abandonment." The sentence may be accurate. It may also avoid saying, "I was hurt when you left." Chiara asks the speaker to say the sentence directly to the person named. A feeling label becomes contact or reveals that it was being used to avoid contact.

Yusuf learns the business version after two renewals. The onboarding checklist is untouched, the screen-share recording has never been watched, and the renewal spreadsheet still rewards rescue. Each unused training session lets the client say the tool is impossible and lets Yusuf say he tried. He moves to a written use criterion: three sessions attended, one workflow installed, support ticket with screenshots before escalation.

Helping is cleanest when use is imaginable. If no one can say what using the help would look like, the offer may already be part of the game.

examples.title: Rebecca Tests the Referral

planSpec.domain: nonprofit case-management meeting with repeated unused referrals
planSpec.audience: a social worker checking whether her rescue plan needs the client to fail
planSpec.stakes: services, dignity, and the helper's self-image are all involved
planSpec.requiredBeat: Rebecca asks the client which referral he will actually use and what barrier blocked the last one, instead of adding a third impressive option.

examples.scenario: "I found another program that might help," Rebecca says, then hears the old script in her own voice. The referral binder is open, the bus pass envelope is still sealed, and the case note screen shows two unused options. Her hand rests on a third brochure. Rebecca has to choose between a more impressive rescue plan and asking which referral can actually be used this week.
examples.whatToDo: Ask which referral the client would use and what blocked the last one. Offer help only after the barrier and use path are named.
examples.whyItMatters: A failed referral can prove the helper tried and the client is hopeless. A usable path tests help without making failure useful to either side.

examples.title: Matteo Interrupts the Model Tour

planSpec.domain: corporate coaching package for an executive who collects frameworks
planSpec.audience: a coach recognizing Psychiatry-style vocabulary touring
planSpec.stakes: expensive insight can replace one hard behavior change
planSpec.requiredBeat: Matteo stops the terminology loop and asks the executive to make one phone call before the next session.

examples.scenario: The leather notebook already has three models boxed in blue ink. Matteo watches the executive connect attachment style, incentives, and family systems while the call list sits untouched beside the next calendar invite. The analysis is fluent. Matteo faces the choice of admiring another framework or asking for one phone call before the next session.
examples.whatToDo: Pause the terminology loop and assign one phone call with a date, person, and first sentence. Make the next session begin with whether the call happened.
examples.whyItMatters: Vocabulary can tour the problem without touching it. A small action tests whether insight is serving change or replacing it.

examples.title: Frida Separates Access from Accountability

planSpec.domain: university accessibility office reviewing missed lab work
planSpec.audience: an adviser separating real accommodation from Wooden Leg deployment
planSpec.stakes: respecting disability while keeping unrelated responsibilities clear
planSpec.requiredBeat: Frida grants the sensory accommodation and still requires the lab safety quiz by a new date.

examples.scenario: The accessibility office window faces a courtyard full of construction noise. Frida reads the accommodation letter while noise-canceling headphones rest beside the missed lab safety quiz. The sensory limit is documented. The safety quiz is still unrelated to the noise exposure. Frida has to choose a response that grants access without erasing accountability.
examples.whatToDo: Approve the sensory accommodation and set a new quiz deadline. State which requirement changed and which requirement remains.
examples.whyItMatters: The limitation deserves respect. The game starts only when a real limit is used to cover a demand it does not touch.

examples.title: Ben Hands Back the Calipers

planSpec.domain: apprenticeship workshop where a trainee keeps acting helpless around measurements
planSpec.audience: a mentor seeing Stupid as a lowered-expectations pattern
planSpec.stakes: the trainee may lose skill and the mentor may enjoy being indispensable
planSpec.requiredBeat: Ben hands back the calipers and waits for the trainee to read the measurement out loud before stepping in.

examples.scenario: You can rescue a bad measurement so quickly that no one learns who needed the rescue. Ben watches a trainee hold digital calipers against a scrap aluminum bar while the measurement worksheet stays blank. "I am terrible at this," the trainee says. Ben predicts the usual handoff. This time he must decide whether to take over or hand the calipers back.
examples.whatToDo: Hand back the calipers and ask the trainee to read the number aloud. Step in only after the attempt is visible.
examples.whyItMatters: Quick rescue lowers the expectation permanently. Waiting preserves dignity and skill by making the measurement belong to the trainee.

examples.title: Chiara Asks for the Direct Sentence

planSpec.domain: therapy group where emotion words replace actual contact
planSpec.audience: a facilitator recognizing Greenhouse in polished self-observation
planSpec.stakes: the group can admire insight while no risk is taken
planSpec.requiredBeat: Chiara asks the speaker to say the sentence directly to the person named, not about the feeling category.

examples.scenario: What happens when every feeling has a label before anyone has felt it in the room? Chiara sits in a circle of chairs near a tissue box and a handwritten feeling list. A member says, "I am noticing abandonment activation around Alex." Chiara must decide whether to praise the insight or ask for the direct sentence to Alex.
examples.whatToDo: Ask the member to say the sentence to Alex in plain words. Keep the feeling label available, but do not let it replace contact.
examples.whyItMatters: Greenhouse keeps feeling observed behind glass. Direct speech tests whether the label supports experience or protects against it.

examples.title: Yusuf Writes the Use Criterion

planSpec.domain: customer-success manager with a client who ignores onboarding then blames the tool
planSpec.audience: a professional helper whose role invites endless rescue
planSpec.stakes: renewal revenue can hide a repeated help-failure game
planSpec.requiredBeat: Yusuf notices that each unused training session lets both sides keep their story, then moves to a written use criterion.

examples.scenario: Two renewals later in the customer-success review, Yusuf sees that the unused onboarding call was not an accident. The onboarding checklist is blank, the screen-share recording has no views, and the renewal spreadsheet still rewards rescue. The client keeps blaming the tool after skipping training. Yusuf writes a use criterion before the next escalation.
examples.whatToDo: Set written criteria: sessions attended, workflow installed, and screenshot-backed ticket before escalation. Make help measurable before adding more help.
examples.whyItMatters: Unused help can prove the client is impossible and the helper diligent. Use criteria stop both sides from profiting from another failed rescue.

questions.prompt: A social worker keeps offering referrals that the client never uses, then feels proven blameless when each plan fails. What game shape fits?
choices: I'm Only Trying to Help You, because failed help becomes useful to the helper.
Wooden Leg, because every unused referral proves disability.
Greenhouse, because the client is using too many emotion words.
questions.explanation: The key is the helper's payoff from failed help. Wooden Leg concerns limitation as exemption, while Greenhouse concerns vocabulary replacing experience.

questions.prompt: A coach's client can explain three models but has not made one necessary call. What is the best intervention?
choices: Introduce a fourth model that better fits the client's style.
Ask for one named phone call before the next session.
Tell the client that insight is useless.
questions.explanation: A concrete call tests whether language is producing movement. More models may extend the tour, while dismissing insight misses that insight can still be useful.

questions.prompt: An accessibility adviser sees a real sensory limitation and an unrelated missed safety quiz. Which response fits the distinction?
choices: Deny the accommodation until all missed work is complete.
Grant the accommodation and set a new date for the safety quiz.
Waive every requirement to avoid ableist suspicion.
questions.explanation: The response respects the real limit and preserves unrelated accountability. Denial punishes the limitation; blanket waiver lets the limitation cover what it does not touch.

questions.prompt: In an apprenticeship workshop, a mentor always takes the digital calipers back when a trainee says, "I'm bad at numbers," and the worksheet stays blank. What should the mentor try next?
choices: Take over faster so the trainee is not embarrassed.
Stop teaching measurement because the trainee lacks ability.
Hand the calipers back and wait for the trainee to read the number aloud.
questions.explanation: The visible attempt prevents rescue from lowering expectations. Taking over reinforces helplessness, and quitting turns a performance of inability into a permanent verdict.

questions.prompt: In a therapy group, someone labels a feeling precisely but never speaks to the person involved. What does Greenhouse warn about?
choices: Emotional vocabulary can become a glass wall between insight and contact.
Emotion words are always fake and should be banned.
Group members should interpret each other without direct speech.
questions.explanation: Greenhouse is about vocabulary replacing lived contact. The words may be accurate; the problem is using them to avoid the direct sentence.

questions.prompt: A software client skips training, blames the tool, and gets more rescue calls before every renewal. What should the customer-success manager add?
choices: More rescue calls so the client feels supported.
A written use criterion before escalation.
A public accusation that the client is refusing help.
questions.explanation: Use criteria make help measurable. More rescue repeats the failed-help cycle, while accusation may be satisfying but does not create a usable path.

questions.prompt: A coach, case manager, or customer-success lead keeps receiving proof that they tried hard while the client stays stuck. Why must the professional be included in the diagnosis of helping games?
choices: Because the helper may receive proof of diligence, innocence, or indispensability from the pattern.
Because professionals are usually more responsible than clients.
Because clients cannot create patterns without permission.
questions.explanation: Helping games often pay the helper too. The point is not to blame professionals more, but to see how the role itself can hide a payoff.

questions.prompt: A real limitation is used to avoid a responsibility unrelated to that limitation. Which phrase best captures the careful reading?
choices: The limitation is fake.
The responsibility should disappear because any limit applies everywhere.
The limit may be real, and the game is in its deployment beyond its actual reach.
questions.explanation: The careful reading protects real limits while naming misuse. Calling the limit fake is cruel; treating it as universal exemption erases accountability.

questions.prompt: Before offering another impressive resource, a helper asks, "What would count as using this?" Why is that a strong move?
choices: It proves the helper is skeptical and detached.
It turns help from a performance into a testable path.
It makes the recipient responsible for every failure.
questions.explanation: A use criterion makes help concrete. The point is not skepticism or blame; it is preventing another offer whose failure benefits the pattern.

reviewCards.front: A helper keeps offering plans that fail, then feels blameless. What should you check?
reviewCards.back: Check whether failed help is useful to the helper. If failure proves diligence or superiority, the offer may be part of I'm Only Trying to Help You.

reviewCards.front: How do you read Wooden Leg carefully?
reviewCards.back: Respect the real limitation, then ask whether it is being used to cover a responsibility unrelated to that limitation. The game is in the deployment, not the disability.

reviewCards.front: What is Greenhouse in a therapy group?
reviewCards.back: It is using polished feeling language to observe experience while avoiding direct contact or change. The antidote is a plain sentence to the person involved.

reviewCards.front: Why can rescue harm skill in a workshop?
reviewCards.back: Fast rescue can lower expectations permanently and make the mentor indispensable. Waiting for a visible attempt protects both dignity and learning.

reviewCards.front: What should a helper ask before adding more help?
reviewCards.back: Ask what would count as the other person using it. If no one can answer, the next offer may only feed the failed-help pattern.

implementationPlan.coreSkill: Learn to make help testable. A professional role can hide the helper's payoff, so both sides need a visible path for what using the help would mean.

ifThenPlans.plan: If two referrals have gone unused, then ask what blocked the last one before offering another resource.
If insight language circles the same avoided action, then assign one observable behavior before the next meeting.
If a real limit is documented, then grant the related accommodation and state which unrelated responsibilities remain.
If a client skips training and asks for rescue, then set written use criteria before escalation.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Before your next offer of help, write the sentence: This help will be used if blank. Fill in the blank with a visible action.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: For one week, review three helping moments. For each, note what the recipient would do if the help worked and what you would get if it failed.

memorableLines.why: It captures the difference between a usable offer and a helper performance.

memorableLines.text: The helper is part of the game.
memorableLines.why: It states the chapter's central reversal in one plain line.

memorableLines.text: Helping is cleanest when use is imaginable.
memorableLines.why: It gives a practical test for every professional example.
